children: Cintas
fiscal first-quarter revenue that topped Wall Street expectations Wednesday, while adjusted earnings also came in ahead of estimates as margins expanded.

Revenue rose 11% to $3.01 billion from $2.72 billion a year earlier, beating the Wall Street consensus estimate of $2.98 billion. Organic revenue growth was 8.9%, which adjusts for acquisitions, currency fluctuations and differences in the number of workdays.
Adjusted earnings were $1.39 a share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.36. The adjusted figure excludes $14.4 million in expenses related to Cintas'
proposed acquisition of UniFirst. Those costs reduced earnings by $0.03 a share.
Shares of Cintas
were little changed in premarket trading Wednesday. As of Tuesday's close, the stock had gained 5.7% this year.
Margin expansion adds to growth
For investors, the quarter showed Cintas

pairing high-single-digit organic growth with improving profitability. Gross margin expanded by 120 basis points while operating margin increased by 90 basis points. The company also raised its full-year revenue and adjusted earnings forecasts, suggesting management expects the momentum to continue despite costs associated with its pending UniFirst transaction.
Net income rose to $551.7 million, or $1.36 a share, from $491.1 million, or $1.20 a share.

Gross margin increased 13.7% to $1.55 billion. Gross margin represented 51.5% of revenue, up from 50.3% a year earlier. Operating income rose 15.2% to $711.9 million while operating margin increased to 23.6% from 22.7%.
Cintas
, best known for its workplace uniform rental business, also provides mats, towels, restroom supplies, first-aid and safety products, fire extinguishers and other workplace services.
Cintas raises full-year forecast
Cintas

raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $12.15 billion to $12.27 billion from its previous range of $12.10 billion to $12.25 billion. The new forecast represents growth of 7.9% to 8.9% from fiscal 2026.

The company also increased its adjusted earnings forecast to $5.45 to $5.54 a share from $5.36 to $5.50. The outlook excludes nonrecurring transaction costs related to the proposed UniFirst acquisition.
“We are pleased with our start to fiscal 2027,” Chief Executive Todd Schneider said in the earnings announcement.
Cintas

said its annual revenue guidance excludes the expected effects of the UniFirst acquisition and assumes no additional acquisitions. The forecast also assumes constant foreign exchange rates. Fiscal 2027 has one more workday than fiscal 2026.
UniFirst deal remains under review
Cintas
said it continues to work with the Federal Trade Commission as the agency reviews its proposed acquisition of UniFirst. The company expects the transaction to close before the end of calendar 2026.
The proposed transaction resulted in $14.4 million of expenses during the quarter. Excluding those costs, adjusted earnings increased 15.8% from a year earlier.
Cintas

also continued returning cash to shareholders. The company paid $208.8 million in quarterly dividends on Sept. 15 and said share repurchases during the fiscal first quarter and through Sept. 22 totaled $544.7 million.

title: Cintas tops revenue estimate, raises fiscal 2027 outlook
